title: Polynomial-Time Computability of Tape Choice
statement: For every finite-state binary Turing machine $M$ and every binary code for its optional states, the function that maps a bit string to the work fragment selected by its encoded work ordinal is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
A binary code is given for the optional states of $M$
replaced: For every source machine and state code, the work-family tape choice is polynomial-time computable: finite selection over the per-tape fragment functions, driven by the native unary quotient and remainder of the work ordinal, including the empty zero-tape family.
